newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to extend beef ban to some French products.
newsitem.headline: Germany to extend beef ban to some French products.

text.p: Germany said on Friday it planned to ban the import and use of selected beef and sheep products from France and Britain as part of measures to protect German consumers against mad cow disease.

A draft directive will be put before the cabinet next month forbidding the import or use of brains, spinal cord and eyes from French cattle over six months old and French or British sheep over 12 months old.
"This measure implements for Germany regulations which these countries have already applied to their own areas," a Health Ministry spokesman told a government news conference.
Germany has been at the forefront of measures to restrict the export of British beef to stop brain-wasting bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) spreading to humans.
It already maintains a national ban on imports of British beef which goes beyond an EU ban on almost all exports of beef from Britain.

The ban on sheep products was a protective measure based on scientific evidence that the fatal human equivalent of BSE, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), might be transferable to humans from sheep, the ministry said.
Brains, spinal cord and eyes account for only a tiny share of meat imports and are used in cosmetics and in technical applications as well as the food industry.
British scientists said this week they had found more evidence that mad cow disease, most prevalent in Britain, could spread to people.
Their research published on Wednesday found a new variant of CJD in humans left traces very similar to BSE.
